variables.reason: The retrieved record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness gives canonical_quantity 'arithmetic mean roughness' with symbols Ra and definition 'Mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level', which exactly matches the ledger's 'first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations'. The record lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, demonstrating Ra has only the length base dimension. Therefore the candidate vector (L=1, all others 0) is fully supported: the single nonzero coordinate is length and all other base exponents are zero.

The retrieved record pq_peak_to_valley_height defines 'mean peak-to-valley roughness height' with symbols including kt and states 'any height difference retains length dimension' and si_unit: m. This directly corresponds to the ledger's 'peak-to-valley height' and confirms it is purely a length quantity; thus the proposed L=1, others 0 vector is correct.

The record pq_rms_roughness_height corresponds to 'root-mean-square roughness height' (symbols k_rms), defined as the RMS fluctuation of surface height; it reports si_unit: m and si_dimension L. This matches the ledger definition and supports the candidate vector with L=1 and all other exponents zero.

The record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (symbols Sk) as the 'Third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution' and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This matches the ledger's Sk description (third central moment normalized by k_rms^3) and confirms every base exponent is zero, so the candidate all-zero vector is correct.

The record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbols Ku) as the 'Fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution' with si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This corresponds exactly to the ledger's 'kurtosis' entry and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The record pq_effective_surface_slope defines 'effective surface slope' (symbols ES) as 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction' and notes 'A surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is dimensionless' with si_dimension: 1. This justifies ES being dimensionless and confirms the candidate all-zero vector.

The record pq_porosity (symbols Po) defines porosity as a fraction of void area/volume, explicitly dimensionless with si_dimension: 1. This aligns with the ledger's 'surface porosity' and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector proposed.
